pull_request.title: Infrastructure: integrate PR60 token dashboard into main
pull_request.head: codex/token-dashboard-main
pull_request.body:
PR #60 was merged into `codex/overleaf-online-sync` after #59 had already merged into main. Its dashboard replacement was therefore absent from main and from the subsequent main-targeted #61.

Integrate #60’s recorded merge commit `b2dc9e1504cb982a34d792225c4b00db472c4cd7` through an ordinary merge on top of the #61 main revision. This PR targets **main directly** and retains the original reviewed history. The integration is conflict-free; dashboard tools, milestone data and workflows match #60 exactly.

This retires the old progress UI/deployment and restores the cumulative token Pages site with combined/input/output modes, feature markers, exact daily tables and aggregate download. Scientific record validation and all 17 existing scientific/software test commands remain in the separate validation workflow. Pages publishes only after a main merge; PR runs provide previews.

All 328 existing main journal/evidence files—including #61’s dedicated calorimeter accounting—remain byte-identical. Tracking/review data and all existing token owners/counters are preserved. The observed project subtotal remains **552,937,331 tokens across 183 unique dated turns**; this active integration turn and existing historical gaps remain excluded.

Local validation: 33 logging/recovery/documentation tests, 8 usage/site tests and JavaScript mode/keyboard checks pass; 155 paired records validate; project records validate (58 tasks / 31 documents / 19 review rounds); the token site builds successfully. Byte-preservation and whitespace checks pass.

All 28 retained project/review/policy/evidence tests also pass against the integrated snapshot.

PR62 head `229e02aaddfe450af695dc221c624d7eaaf529c7` on
`infrastructure/device-accounting-sync-20261012`; the four unrelated untracked
token-gate files remain untouched. PR63 merged into main as

ownership correction. GitHub showed PR62 as mergeable with passing old-dashboard
CI, but that did not validate the newly introduced token-site workflow.

Read the changed repository instructions and current token/project validation
guides. An ordinary merge in an isolated checkout was conflict-free but the new
token collector failed against the combined records. The branch therefore needs
a compatibility correction, despite having no textual merge conflict. The
repository requires ordinary merges, so shared history is preserved.
